questions.stem: The change from the solid state to the gaseous state:
options: Is obtained at a pressure higher than that of the triple point in the (P, T) diagram
questions.explanation: No official answer key for this exam — answer worked out. Sublimation occurs below the triple-point pressure and absorbs energy.

questions.stem: A mixture of k gases is placed in a volume V:
options: The pressure of the mixture equals the pressure of each gas
The partial pressures of these gases are identical
The total pressure of the mixture is the sum of the partial pressures of the k gases
The total volume V is the sum of the partial volumes of the k gases
The volume of each gas equals V only if the partial pressures of the k gases are equal
questions.explanation: No official answer key — Dalton's law.

questions.stem: A mass m = 9 g of water (M = 18 g/mol) is introduced into an initially empty hermetic container of volume V = 25 L and brought to T₁ = 70°C. What mass of water remains liquid? Given: saturation pressure of water Psat(70°C) = 0.350 bar, Psat(100°C) = 1 bar. (R = 8.31 SI)
questions.explanation: No official key — worked out. Max vapor: n = PV/RT = 35 000 × 0.025 / (8.31 × 343) ≈ 0.307 mol ≈ 5.5 g. Liquid left = 9 − 5.5 ≈ 3.5 g.

questions.stem: (Continued: 9 g of water in a 25 L hermetic container.) What is the water vapor pressure in this container at 100°C?
questions.explanation: No official key — worked out. If all 0.5 mol vaporizes: P = nRT/V = 0.5 × 8.31 × 373 / 0.025 ≈ 0.62 bar < Psat (1 bar), so all the water is vapor and P = 0.62 bar.

questions.stem: The correct statement is:
options: For an electrolytic solution, the Van't Hoff correction factor is always greater than 1
The equivalent concentration of a solution equals its ionic concentration
The osmolality of an electrolytic solution (α₀ = 0.5) equals its molality
The osmolarity of a molar NaCl solution equals the osmolarity of a molar CaCl₂ solution
questions.explanation: No official key — i = 1 + α(ν − 1) > 1 whenever the solute dissociates.

questions.stem: One liter of solution contains 15 mL of HCl (2 mol/L) and 30 mL of H₂SO₄ (1 mol/L). The electrolytes are totally dissociated. Calculate the osmolarity of the solution.
questions.explanation: No official key — HCl: 0.03 mol × 2 = 60 mosm; H₂SO₄: 0.03 mol × 3 = 90 mosm; total 150 mosm/L.

questions.stem: An aqueous solution of 0.65 mol/L Na₃PO₄ has a dissociation coefficient α₀ = 0.6. What is its osmolarity? The ions in solution are PO₄³⁻ and Na⁺.
An aqueous solution of volume 1 L contains 2.34 g of NaCl (M = 58.5 g) and 3.33 g of CaCl₂ (M = 111 g). What is its ionic strength?
Solvation is due to:
options: The dipolar molecules of the solvent
The high electric permittivity of the solvent
The decrease of the Coulomb force
The strong character of some electrolytes
questions.explanation: No official key — solvation is the surrounding of ions by the dipolar solvent molecules.

questions.stem: The freezing-point depression of a 0.2 mol/L CaCl₂ solution is −0.65°C. What is its degree of dissociation? (Kc = 1.86 °C·osm⁻¹·L)

Two identical cylindrical cells (S = 10 cm², L = 12 cm) are filled with the same molar aqueous solution of a totally dissociated AB electrolyte. When the cells (R) are placed in a Wheatstone bridge (figure), balance is reached for R₁ = 64 Ω, R₂ = 16 Ω. Calculate the resistance R.
questions.explanation: No official key — at balance R × R = R₁ × R₂ = 1024 → R = 32 Ω.

questions.stem: (Continued) Calculate the conductivity of the solution.
questions.explanation: No official key — σ = L / (R·S) = 0.12 / (32 × 10⁻³) = 3.75 S/m.

questions.stem: The correct statement is:
options: Reverse osmosis is the transfer of water through a dialyzing membrane
Two iso-osmotic solutions have the same molar concentration
Osmosis is the transfer of water through a semipermeable membrane
Two isotonic solutions automatically have the same osmolarities
questions.explanation: No official key — definition of osmosis.

questions.stem: The osmotic pressure at 27°C initially exerted between compartments A and B across a semipermeable membrane (figure) is 750 Pa. Assuming water diffuses from A to B, determine the initial osmolarity of compartment B (in osmol/m³). The electrolytes are totally dissociated.
questions.explanation: No official key — Δc = ΔΠ/RT = 750 / (8.31 × 300) ≈ 0.30 osmol/m³. A: 0.6 × 3 = 1.8 osmol/m³. Water goes to the more concentrated side, so B = 1.8 + 0.3 = 2.1 osmol/m³.

questions.stem: In a Donnan experiment, at equilibrium [Na⁺]I = 0.57 osmol/L and [Na⁺]II = 0.714 osmol/L (the protein is in compartment II). Calculate [Cl⁻]II.
questions.explanation: No official key — [Na⁺]I[Cl⁻]I = [Na⁺]II[Cl⁻]II with [Cl⁻]I = [Na⁺]I: [Cl⁻]II = 0.57² / 0.714 ≈ 0.455 osmol/L.

questions.stem: A globular particle, initially at x = 10 cm from the rotor axis of a centrifuge, undergoes ultracentrifugation at 50 000 rpm. Calculate the distance it travels in 75 min, given its Svedberg constant is 10 S.
questions.explanation: No official key — x = x₀·e^(sω²t); ω = 5236 rad/s, sω²t = 10⁻¹² × 2.74×10⁷ × 4500 ≈ 0.123 → x ≈ 11.31 cm, distance ≈ 13 mm.

questions.stem: Three identical charges q = +4 µC are placed at the vertices of an equilateral triangle ABC of side a = 1 m. Calculate the energy of their configuration. (k = 9×10⁹ SI)
questions.explanation: No official key — U = 3kq²/a = 3 × 9×10⁹ × 16×10⁻¹² = 0.432 J.

questions.stem: Consider the electric circuit in the figure. Determine the equivalent resistance (in ohms) between points x and y.
questions.explanation: No official key, and the scan has handwriting over some resistor values. Upper branch: the three parallel resistors (≈2 Ω) + 16 Ω ≈ 18 Ω; lower branch: 9 Ω ∥ 4.5 Ω = 3 Ω, + 6 Ω = 9 Ω. 18 ∥ 9 = 6 Ω.

questions.stem: During a strong stimulus, the stimulation time of a nerve fiber equals chronaxie/5. The threshold intensity of this stimulus as a function of the rheobase (I₀) is:
questions.explanation: No official key — Lapicque: I = I₀(1 + τ/t) = I₀(1 + 5) = 6 I₀.

questions.stem: The correct statement is:
options: The depolarization–polarization interface in a muscle fiber is equivalent to a fixed electric dipole
The vectorcardiogram represents the variation of the heart's electric field at the precordial leads
The precordial leads are 6 bipolar leads
Atrial myocardium contraction appears at the T wave
The sides of Einthoven's triangle are obtained by the three bipolar limb leads (D1, D2 and D3)
questions.explanation: No official key — the dipole moves, precordial leads are unipolar, and the T wave is ventricular repolarization.
